'''Jerzy Adam Gracjan Vetulani''' ({{IPA|pl|ˈjɛ.ʐɨ ˈa.dam ˈɡrat͡s.jan ˌvɛ.tu.ˈla.ɲi}}; 21 January 1936 – 6 April 2017) was a Polish [[neuroscientist]], [[Psychopharmacology|psychopharmacologist]] and [[biochemist]], [[professor]] of [[natural sciences]], member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Polish Academy of Learning]], between 1956 and 2017 employee at the [[Institute of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences]] in [[Kraków]], where he was head of the Department of Biochemistry (1976–2006), deputy director for Science Affairs (1994–2002) and vice chairman of the Scientific Council (2003–2017).<ref name="pan">{{cite web| url = http://czlonkowie.pan.pl/czlonkowie/sites/Biogram.html?id=3812| title = Jerzy Vetulani| access-date = 7 April 2017| publisher = Polska Akademia Nauk| language    = pl| archive-date = 24 August 2017| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170824145533/http://czlonkowie.pan.pl/czlonkowie/sites/Biogram.html?id=3812| url-status = dead}}</ref> He published more than 240 original [[Academic publishing#Scholarly paper|research papers]] in [[Peer review|peer-review]] [[Academic journal|journals]]. While a Research Associate Professor at the [[Vanderbilt University]], together with [[Fridolin Sulser]] in 1975 he formulated an early hypothesis of the mechanism of action of [[Antidepressant|antidepressant drugs]], suggesting  that [[Downregulation and upregulation|downregulation]] of beta-[[adrenergic receptor]]s is responsible for their effects.<ref>Sulser F., Vetulani J.: ''Action of various antidepressant treatments reduces reactivity of noradrenergic cyclic AMP generating system in limbic forebrain'', "[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]", 257, 1975.</ref><ref>{{cite book |title= The Antidepressant Era |url= https://archive.org/details/antidepressanter00heal |url-access= registration |last= Healy |first= David |author-link= David Healy (psychiatrist) |year= 1997 |publisher= Harvard University Press |isbn= 0-674-03958-0 |page= [https://archive.org/details/antidepressanter00heal/page/162 162]}}</ref> In 1983, he received {{ill|Anna-Monika Prize|de|Anna-Monika Prize|display=1}} for research on the mechanisms of the [[electroconvulsive therapy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://anna-monika-stiftung.de/?p=498| title=1982 / 1983 – 2nd Prize (Vetulani)| date=24 February 2014| publisher=Anna Monika Stiftung| access-date = 11 January 2016}}</ref> Beside [[Major depressive disorder|depression]], his research interests included [[memory]], [[addiction]] and [[neurodegeneration]]. According to [[Andrzej Mikołaj Pilc|Andrzej Pilc]], he was one of the most frequently cited Polish scientists in the field of [[biomedicine]] between 1965 and 2001.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://biotechnologia.pl/biotechnologia/najczesciej-cytowani-polscy-naukowcy-z-nauk-biomedycznych,12088| title = Najczęściej cytowani naukowcy oraz prace naukowe w Polsce, raport za lata 1965 – 2001 na podstawie bazy "Science Citation Index" dotyczącej wszystkich światowych publikacji| access-date = 25 December 2018| publisher = biotechnologia.pl| last = Pilc| first = Andrzej | language    = pl}}</ref>

He was a [[Popular science|popularizer]] and [[Science communication|communicator]] of science, between 1981 and 2002 the editor-in-chief of the ''[[Wszechświat]]'' magazine. He ran popular lectures and authored several popular science books. Since 2010 he ran a blog ''Piękno neurobiologii'' (''The Beauty of Neuroscience'') and [[social media]] channels.

In the [[Polish People's Republic]], he was an activist of the [[Union of Polish Youth]], announcer at [[Piwnica pod Baranami]] cabaret (1954–1961) and a member of the [[Association of Atheists and Freethinkers]]. In 1978 he was registered as an [[unofficial collaborator]] of the [[Security Service (Poland)|Security Service]]. From 1980, he was a member of the [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]]. For about half a century he maintained an acquaintance with [[Pope John Paul II|Karol Wojtyła]], who was chosen a pope in 1978.

He argued against the [[war on drugs]], in favor of the [[Legality of cannabis|legalization of marijuana]] and wide [[Drug liberalization|depenalization of drugs]] for adult users, criticizing Poland and other countries for their [[drug policy|drug policies]], that he considered repressive. A candidate in the [[2002 Polish local elections|Kraków presidential elections]] in 2002, he did not succeed. Between 2010 and 2015 he performed in the ''[[Talking Dog|Gadający Pies]]'' (''The Talking Dog'') live magazine.

An [[Honorary degree|honorary doctor]] of the [[Medical University of Silesia]] and the [[Medical University of Łódź]], honorary fellow of Indian Academy of Neurosciences and Oxford Neurological Society, he received several dozen awards, including state distinctions, among them the Knight's Cross of [[Order of Polonia Restituta|Polonia Restituta]].

== Biography ==
=== Social background ===
[[File:Rodzina Vetulanich w Sanoku.jpg|200px|thumb|right|[[Adam Vetulani]], first to the left, with his grandmother, mother and siblings, c. 1910]]
His father, [[Adam Vetulani]], came from [[Sanok]], and was a professor at the [[Jagiellonian University]], head of the Department of Canon Law; the son of [[Roman Vetulani]] and Elżbieta née Kunachowicz (who came from an impoverished [[Polish landed gentry|landowning]] family).<ref>{{cite book| title = Adam Vetulani (1901–1976). Historyk prawa polskiego i kanonicznego| last = Biliński| first = Piotr| publisher = Jagiellonian University Press| year = 2023}}</ref> He had daughter [[Kristine Vetulani-Belfoure|Kristine]] (born 1924), Jerzy's older sister. Jerzy Vetulani's mother, [[Irena Latinik-Vetulani|Irena Vetulani née Latinik]], was a biologist and researcher at the Department of Comparative Anatomy at the Jagiellonian University, daughter of [[Franciszek Latinik]], Polish Army General; and Helena née Stiasny-Strzelbicka. Jerzy Vetulani's uncles were: [[Kazimierz Vetulani|Kazimierz]], [[Zygmunt Vetulani (diplomat)|Zygmunt]] and [[Tadeusz Vetulani]], his closest aunt was Maria Vetulani (“Maryla”; 1895–1945), a bank clerk; his further aunts were [[Zofia Vetulani|Zofia]], [[Maria Vetulani de Nisau|Maria]] and [[Cecylia Vetulani]]; his paternal cousins were Witold de Nisau, Wanda and [[Zygmunt Vetulani (computer scientist)|Zygmunt Vetulani]], and his maternal cousins were [[Irena Popiel|Irena]] and [[Andrzej Popiel]], and [[Janusz Rieger|Janusz]] and Jerzy Rieger.

=== 1936–1952: Early years and rebellion===
[[File:Irena i Jerzy Vetulani.jpg|Jerzy Vetulani with his mother [[Irena Latinik-Vetulani]], 1938|thumb|250px]]
[[File:Adam Vetulani z synem Jerzym lata 30.jpg|Jerzy Vetulani with his father Adam Vetulani, c. 1939|thumb|200px]]
He was born on 21 January 1936<ref name="kto">{{cite book| title = Kto jest kim w polskiej medycynie. Informator biograficzny| publisher = Wydawnictwo Interpress| place = Warsaw| year = 1987| page = 696| isbn = 83-2232339-5}}</ref> at the private gynecological hospital at Garncarska Street in [[Kraków]], [[Second Polish Republic|Poland]]. In 1938 his younger brother Jan was born. The family lived in an apartment on the ground floor of the {{ill|house of professors of the Jagiellonian University at Plac Inwalidów|pl|Dom mieszkalny profesorów Uniwersytetu Jagiellońskiego (plac Inwalidów)|display=1}}, employing a maid, cook and Olga Rutter, a child educator.

As Nazi Germany [[Invasion of Poland|invaded Poland]] in September 1939, Adam Vetulani took part in the defense war. With his unit, he went to Romania and then to France, where he also [[Battle of France|fought on the front]]. Eventually he was interned in Switzerland, where he spent the rest of the war organizing school camps for Polish soldiers.<ref>{{cite book| author = Adam Vetulani| title = Poza płomieniami wojny. Internowani w Szwajcarii 1940-45| publisher = Wydawnictwo Ministerstwa Obrony Narodowej| place = Warsaw| year = 1976}}</ref> The correspondence sent to the occupied Poland was signed by the Fraulein Kupfer alias.{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| p=17}}

After the German army entered Kraków, Irena Vetulani and her sons had to leave the apartment. They were given forty-eight hours to move, with the possibility of keeping movable property.{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| p=15}} They moved to the premises at Garncarska Street 4, where Józefa Onitsch, the wife of General [[Zygmunt Zieliński (1858–1925)|Zygmunt Zieliński]], gave them refuge. The family was supported by Adam Vetulani's brother, [[Tadeusz Vetulani|Tadeusz]], who has been living in Kraków during the war. Irena Latinik-Vetulani, thanks to her good knowledge of German, took up a job as a translator in the spirit monopoly. Jerzy and Jan Vetulani remained in war years under the care of their mother who raised both sons “in a patriotic sense of honor”.{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=495}} Every Sunday at home there was a “[[Mystery play|mystery]]” and the family used to sing Polish Catholic patriotic song ''[[Boże, coś Polskę]]''.{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| p=18}} In his childhood, Jerzy Vetulani was a religious boy; he served as an [[Altar server|altar boy]] at [[St. Mary's Basilica, Kraków|St. Mary's Basilica]].

Jerzy Vetulani recalled the war years as interesting, full of fascinating activity and exploring the surrounding world, undermining the collective, martyrological picture of despair and misery. Together with his younger brother Jan and their friend from the tenement house, Andrzej Mirocki, they founded an insect gatherer club. They gathered a diverse collection of butterflies.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.focus.pl/czlowiek/macanie-swiata-9193| title = Macanie świata| publisher = Focus| access-date = 29 March 2017| author = Katarzyna Sroczyńska| date = 18 March 2013| language = pl| archive-date = 29 March 2017| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170329141632/http://www.focus.pl/czlowiek/macanie-swiata-9193| url-status = dead}}</ref> Irena Latinik-Vetulani never allowed her children witness a street execution.

Jerzy Vetulani began his education in 1942 and immediately entered the second class of [[Education in Poland during World War II|secret sets]] led by Mrs. Iwiczowa, as he was already able to read and write.{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=495}} From 1948 he attended the {{ill|Henryk Sienkiewicz High School in Kraków|pl|IV Gimnazjum i Liceum im. Henryka Sienkiewicza w Krakowie|display=1}}, and then, after his liquidation, [[Bartłomiej Nowodworski High School]],<ref name="poszedlemdojedynki">{{cite book| chapter = Poszedłem do „jedynki”, która zawsze była i została „jedynką”. Z Jerzym Vetulanim rozmawiają Natalia Jurek, Jan Kłapa i Szymon Sapalski| url = https://www.franekvetulani.eu/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Vetulani_Nowodworek.pdf| title = Nowodworek z pamięci. Uczniowie, absolwenci i nauczyciele we wspomnieniach, biografiach i anegdotach| volume = 2| others = Wojciech Strokowski (ed.)| publisher = Wydawnictwo Fall, I Liceum Ogólnokształcące im. Bartłomieja Nowodworskiego w Krakowie| pages = 122–135| place = Kraków| year = 2021| archive-date = 15 June 2023| access-date = 21 November 2025| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230615145457/https://www.franekvetulani.eu/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Vetulani_Nowodworek.pdf| url-status = bot: unknown}}</ref> where he passed [[matura]] in 1952, obtaining a certificate with a distinction for best pupils.<ref name="sla">{{cite web| url = http://dokument.slam.katowice.pl/monogram.asp?idm=2746| title = Doktorzy honoris causa – Jerzy Adam Vetulani| access-date = 22 April 2012| author = Zbigniew Herman| publisher = Śląski Uniwersytet Medyczny| language = pl| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110405094906/http://dokument.slam.katowice.pl/monogram.asp?idm=2746| archive-date = 5 April 2011| url-status = dead}}</ref>

Already as a teenager, Jerzy Vetulani has completely walked away from religion. He described himself from a young age as “a rebel who did a lot of things in spite of his parents.” At the age of twelve he enrolled in the [[Union of Polish Youth]]. He was removed from the organization as a result of a typo in the school newspaper article.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.gazetakrakowska.pl/artykul/397516,na-kanapce-vetulaniego-siadywal-karol-wojtyla,id,t.html| title = Na kanapce Vetulaniego siadywał Karol Wojtyła| access-date= 26 May 2012 | author = Małgorzata Iskra| publisher = [[Gazeta Krakowska]]| date = 29 April 2011| language = pl}}</ref> In the text he mistakenly and unconsciously, instead of “the basis of socialism” (''podstawy socjalizmu''), he wrote “the washers of socialism” (''podsrawy socjalizmu'').{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=500}} Later he joined the [[Association of Atheists and Freethinkers]]. He belonged to the {{ill|Revolutionary Youth Union (Poland)|pl|Rewolucyjny Związek Młodzieży|display=2}},{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| p=32}} a formation of idealistic communists who were striving for reform of Polish communist system that they considered defective.

=== 1952–1973: Studies, cabaret, Institute of Pharmacology ===
[[File:Vetulani J 1960s.jpg|right|200px|thumb|Jerzy Vetulani in the 1960s]]
In 1952 he began his studies in biology at the [[Jagiellonian University]] (specializing in animal physiology),<ref name="sla" /> which he completed in 1957, defending his thesis on the effects of ascorbic acid on rabbit blood.<ref name="kto" /><ref name="cv">{{cite web| url = http://vetulani.wordpress.com/o-mnie/cv/| title = Jerzy Vetulani – CV| date = 16 May 2012| access-date = 17 May 2012 | publisher = vetulani.wordpress.com| language = pl}}</ref> In March 1956, he began a volunteer internshipat at the [[Institute of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences|Department of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences]] (later renamed the Institute of Pharmacology), where he has been working since, until the end of his life. Janusz Supniewski was head of the department at that time.<ref name="sla" /> In 1957, after obtaining master's degree, Vetulani was hired as an assistant.

Later, also at the Jagiellonian University, he studied chemistry (specializing in theoretical chemistry).<ref name="sla" /> He graduated in 1963.<ref name="kto" /> As an exchange student he spent seven weeks in [[Swansea]], where he worked at the [[British Iron and Steel Research Association]].{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| pp=62–63}} He rented a room at a senior Welsh marriage and studied English intensively; every day he bought an edition of ''[[Daily Mirror]]'' and underlined unknown words, that he later learned.

He was one of the founders and permanent regulars of the [[Piwnica pod Baranami]] cabaret. In the mid-1950s, together with a group of friends: Edmund Jarosz, [[Bronisław Chromy]] and Lala Skąpska, he took part in the demolition of the basement at Palace Pod Baranami, which soon became room for the cabaret.{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=498}} In 1958, when [[Piotr Skrzynecki]] left for [[Paris]], Vetulani temporarily replaced him as a conference caller.<ref name="piw">{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9cbEtfK4NNA| title = Jerzy Vetulani w Piwnicy pod Baranami| access-date = 22 April 2012| publisher = YouTube| date = 12 March 2012| language = pl}}</ref> It was in Piwnica that he met his future wife, Maria Pająk, whose appearance at the time he compared to [[Marina Vlady]]'s.{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| pp=43–44}} They married on 8 July 1963. Soon after that their sons Marek and [[Tomasz Vetulani|Tomasz]] were born, respectively in 1964 and 1965. They also had four grandchildren.<ref>{{cite journal| last = Kołodziej| first = Beata| title = Krakowianie: Rzymskie wakacje, rzymskie zimy| journal = Dziennik Polski, Kronika Krakowska | page = 2| date = 17 March 2012}}</ref>

{{quote box|align=right|width=25em|quote=I befriended all the people from ''Piwnica'' — even the charming, but unbearable Jurek Vetulani, who kept teasing me that I was old and fat, and when I entered the Piwnica, he screamed blue murder: “Turn off the light, turn off the light, the rotten wood shall shine now!”.|source=– [[Kika Szaszkiewiczowa]] about the friendship in [[Piwnica pod Baranami]]<ref>{{cite book|last = Szaszkiewiczowa| first = Kika| title = Podwójne życie Szaszkiewiczowej| publisher = Wydawnictwo Literackie| place = Kraków| year = 2011| page = 244| isbn = 978-83-08-04790-3}}</ref>}}

In 1955–1962 he acted as a speaker at the Kraków Student Film Discussion Club.<ref name="pan" /> Jerzy Vetulani admitted that “it was a good thing” because “it taught him to speak short, interesting and fast”.<ref name="piw" /> In 1972 he was a scientific consultant for the film ''Illumination'' directed by [[Krzysztof Zanussi]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://filmpolski.pl/fp/index.php/12128| title = Iluminacja| access-date = 11 April 2012| publisher = Filmpolski.pl| language = pl}}</ref>

After the death of his brother, who drowned during a canoeing on the [[Dunajec|Dunajec River]] in 1965, he mobilized to begin work on his Ph.D. dissertation.{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=501}} He obtained Ph.D. degree in natural sciences in 1966 from Ludwik Hirszfeld Institute of Immunology and Experimental Therapy of the Polish Academy of Sciences upon dissertation ''The action of isoxazole and pyrazole derivatives on the metabolism of the animal system'' prepared under the direction of Professor Józef Hano.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://nauka-polska.pl/dhtml/raporty/ludzieNauki?rtype=opis&objectId=47469&lang=pl| title = Jerzy Vetulani at the "Ludzie nauki" Database| publisher = nauka-polska.pl| access-date = 7 April 2017| language = pl}}</ref> In the same year went to Great Britain for one year Riker scholarship. In the UK he worked on mastering spectrofluorimetric methods at the [[University of Cambridge]] under the direction of [[Arnold Burgen]].<ref name="cv" /> During his stay in Cambridge, he encountered Bożena Puchalska and [[Juliusz Hibner]].

After returning to Poland he started work in the field of psychopharmacology under the direction of [[Jerzy Maj]].

===1973–1989: In the orbit of world science. Opposition ===
After submitting a habilitation dissertation, he left to the [[United States]] for almost two years. There, he worked from 1973 to 1975 as Research Associate Professor at the [[Vanderbilt University]].<ref name="cv" /> He gained international recognition after the discovery in 1975, with [[Fridolin Sulser]], of β-downregulation by chronic administration of antidepressants and the formulation of β-downregulation hypothesis as a mechanism of action of antidepressants. The work on this subject, published by Vetulani and Sulser in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', became citation classic, receiving 580 vocations by 2007.<ref name="cv" />

After his mother's death, he and his family decided to return to Poland. Vetulani received his habilitation degree in 1976 (upon work ''Neuroleptics, monoamine oxidase inhibitors and dopamine beta-hydroxylase inhibitors: their actions and synergies''), an associate professor in 1983, and a professor in 1989.<ref name="pan" /> In 1976, he was appointed Head of the Department of Biochemistry at Institute of Pharmacology.{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=524}}

In the 1970s he translated several short stories by [[Ursula le Guin]] for magazine ''[[Przekrój]]''. In ''Przekrój'' he also published short articles on his stay in the United States. Back in the 1960s he was offered regular work in ''Przekrój'' by its long-time editor-in-chief [[Marian Eile]], but refused due to lack of possibility to combine scientific career with a full-time job as a columnist in a weekly.

Since 1978 he has regularly collaborated with the [[Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche]] (CNR, National Research Council) in Rome. On behalf of the Institute of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences he was a coordinator of the joint research program of his home Institute with the Istituto di Biology Cellulare and Neurobiology (IBCN). When visiting Rome, he usually received an audience with [[John Paul II]], who was a student of his father and friend of the family. Also in 1978 he was registered as [[Security Service (Poland)|Security Service]] [[unofficial collaborator]].{{sfn|Kubisiowska|2022|p=340}} His codename was "Laborant" and his operational number was 19856.{{sfn|Kubisiowska|2022|p=340}} From the 1970s he was in a close relationship with [[Sylwia Tomecka-Suchoń]].{{sfn|Kubisiowska|2022|pp=375–377}} They befriended Małgorzata and [[Jacek Ostaszewski|Jacek Ostaszewscy]].{{sfn|Kubisiowska|2022|pp=375–377}} Since the mid-1970s he suffered from [[glaucoma]].{{sfn|Kubisiowska|2022|pp=378–382}}

In 1983 Jerzy Vetulani received {{ill|Anna-Monika Prize|de|Anna-Monika Prize|display=1}} (2nd class) for his research on the mechanism of [[Electroconvulsive therapy|electroconvulsion]]. In years 1981–2002 he was the editor-in-chief of ''[[Wszechświat]]'', one of the oldest Polish popular science magazines. He was also the editor-in-chief of the ''Polish Journal of Pharmacology and Pharmacy'' (1993–1996). He obtained the title of associate professor in 1983 and the title of full professor in 1989.

From 1980 he was an activist in the [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]] movement.<ref name=pan /> He was a member of the Solidarity Work Committee to the Department and Branches of the Polish Academy of Sciences in Kraków and was the 56th member of the Coordinating Commission for Science. In 1987–1989 he was a member of the Solidarity's Board of the [[Lesser Poland|Małopolska Region]], at the end of that period, from 1989 to 1990 he was a member of the Presidium of the Board. He mainly dealt with programming matters and advised organization's authorities in the region. In the work for Solidarity he took advantage of the position of the editor-in-chief of a scientific magazine; during the [[martial law in Poland|martial law]] he smuggled a letter from Solidarity's region authorities from Poland to Vatican, where he passed it to pope John Paul II.{{sfn|Kobos|2007| p=494}} He thought this smuggling was possible only because he wasn't searched, as a person at such an important position, and accompanied in his travel to Italy then by Mieczysław Czuma, editor-in-chief of ''Przekrój''.

=== 1989–2006: Late career and social activity ===
Jerzy Vetulani was a member of [[Solidarity Citizens' Committee]] (1989–1990) and Kraków Solidarity Club (1994–1995).

Between 1992 and 1998 he was a member of the Collegium Internationale Neuro-Psychopharmacologicum. In 1999–2001 he was the President of the [[Polish Neuroscience Society]].<ref name="pan" /> He also introduced Polish term for [[neurofibrillary tangle]]s, which he called ''splątki neurofibrylarne''.<ref>{{cite book|author=Christopher Turner, Anish Bahra, Katia Cikurel|title=Crash Course: Neurologia|year=2007 |publisher=Elsevier Urban&Partner|place=Wrocław|isbn=978-83-60290-71-2|page=118}}</ref>

In 1991 he was appointed a correspondent member of the [[Polish Academy of Learning]]. He was appointed a full member in 1996. He regularly held meetings of the Scientific Cafe at the Polish Academy of Learning at Sławkowska Street 17, as the opening and moderator of the discussions. He was a member of the board of the [[Kraków Society of Friends of Fine Arts]] (2001–2017) and a member of the chapter of the [[Laurel of Kraków of the 21st century]] (also 2001–2017). He was a member of the board of the Society for the Advancement and Promotion of Science and member of the [[Warsaw Scientific Society]] and the European [[Dana Foundation|Dana]] Alliance for the Brain (EDAB). In 2002 he was appointed vice-chairman of the Scientific Council of the Insitiute of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences.

Over the years, his students (many of whom worked in the Department of Biochemistry he led) included [[Irena Nalepa]] (collaboration in the years 1986–2017), [[Piotr Popik]], [[Lucyna Antkiewicz-Michaluk]] (close cooperation in the years 1976–2006), [[Andrzej Mikołaj Pilc|Andrzej Pilc]], [[Krystyna Gołembiowska]], [[Jolanta Zawilska]], [[Marek Sanak]], {{ill|Rafał Ryguła|pl|Rafał Ryguła|display=1}} and [[Dominika Dudek]].

In 2002 he was a founding member of the Forum for Małopolska Association and ran unsuccessfully for the presidency of the city of Kraków, obtaining 2375 votes (1.19%) in the first round of elections.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://wybory2002.pkw.gov.pl/wojt/t1/gw1/w12/m1261.html| title = Wybory samorządowe w Krakowie 2002 – I tura| publisher = Państwowa Komisja Wyborcza| language = pl| access-date = 2 September 2011}}</ref>

In 2008 he was elected a correspondent member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]. Over the years, he held various functions in the academy's structures. He was the secretary of the Committee of Physiological Sciences (1978–1981), chair of the Neurobiology Committee (2007–2011), a member of the Scientific Council of the Institute of Experimental Biology (1993–2007) and the Institute of Experimental and Clinical Medicine (2003–2007) of the Polish Academy of Sciences.<ref name="pan" />

=== 2006–2017: Towards popular science ===
[[File:Jerzy Vetulani TEDx Krakow cropped.jpg|right|250px|thumb|Jerzy Vetulani at TEDxKraków, 2011]]
[[File:Jerzy Vetulani giving a lecture in Gorlice cropped.jpg|right|250px|thumb|Jerzy Vetulani in [[Gorlice]], 2013]]
In 2006, Vetulani left the position of head of the department of biochemistry of the Institute of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences and devoted himself to a large degree to popular science. In this field he was active already in the 1960s when he published short texts in ''Wszechświat'', as a rule signing articles with his own name or with pseudonym J. Latini.<ref name="cv" /> After 2000 he became known for his popular science lectures, which focused on themes connected with the functioning of [[human brain]] and the relationship between neuroscience and various social and cultural aspects. In 1999 he was a lecturer during the Kraków Brain Days, and since 2000 he has performed every year at the Kraków Brain Week organized as a part of World [[Brain Awareness Week]].

Since June 2010 Vetulani ran a [[blog]] titled ''Piękno neurobiologii'' (''The Beauty of Neuroscience'') on [[WordPress]]. There, he published articles on discoveries in the fields of neuroscience and psychopharmacology and comments on the curiosities of the human brain and, additionally, various cultural and social matters.<ref>{{cite book |title= Koniec epoki kredy|last= Pezda|first= Aleksandra|year= 2011|publisher= Agora SA|location= [[Warsaw]]|isbn= 978-83-268-0517-2|pages= 81–82}}</ref> The direct cause of the founding of the site was the removal of Vetulani's column in ''[[Wprost]]'' magazine by the newly elected editor-in-chief [[Tomasz Lis]].<ref name="kul">{{cite web| url = http://ekulczycki.pl/teoria_komunikacji/sylwetka-blogera-naukowego-jerzy-vetulani/| title = Sylwetka blogera naukowego: Jerzy Vetulani| last = Kulczycki| first = Emanuel | publisher = ekulczycki.pl| date = 5 March 2012| language = pl| access-date = 29 February 2012}}</ref> As the main motivator for blogging Vetulani has pointed the desire to share his own knowledge with others. In a 2011 interview he said, “Soon, what's in my brain will kick the bucket, so I have to try to pass on to others as much as I can.”.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://redakcja.mammedia.pl/paper/preview/in-the-gratka/11/1/3/| title = Wywiad z Jerzym Vetulanim| last = Vetulani| first = Franciszek| publisher = In The Gratka| date = January 2011| language = pl| access-date = 29 February 2012| archive-date = 23 May 2013| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130523015615/http://redakcja.mammedia.pl/paper/preview/in-the-gratka/11/1/3/| url-status = dead}}</ref> He chose this form of sharing his texts because of the ability to reach wide group of readers, as well as because of the independence and freedom of content and deadlines.<ref name="kul" /> Since December 2011, he has also run a channel on [[YouTube]], on which has published videos and records of his lectures.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/user/JerzyVetulani?feature=watch| title = Jerzy Vetulani | publisher = YouTube| access-date = 14 November 2012}}</ref> Vetulani published several popular articles on the topic of neuroscience, he has often given interviews for various magazines and appeared in the radio and television, becoming, especially in the last decade of his life, a celebrity in science.

After 1989 Vetulani politically sympathized with the center and the left. He has publicly supported specific candidats for public offices. In the [[2010 Polish presidential election|2010 presidential election]] in both rounds he supported [[Bronisław Komorowski]]<ref>{{cite web| url = http://vetulani.wordpress.com/2010/07/05/nowym-prezydentem-komorowski-czlowiek-godny-na-tym-stanowisku/| title = Nowym prezydentem Komorowski – człowiek godny na tym stanowisku| publisher = vetulani.wordpress.com| date = 5 July 2010| language = pl| access-date = 12 May 2012}}</ref> and in the [[2011 Polish parliamentary election|parliamentary election]] a year later [[Józef Lassota]]. In [[2014 European Parliament election]] he supported [[Jan Hartman (philosopher)|Jan Hartman]], expressing at the same time his solidarity with [[Róża Thun]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v_T6XXLaflc| title = Vetulani popiera Hartmana| publisher = YouTube| date = 21 May 2014| language = pl| access-date = 22 May 2014}}</ref> Prior to the first round of [[2015 Polish presidential election|presidential election in 2015]], he supported [[Janusz Palikot]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45WHLXIOH_w| title = Prof. Jerzy Vetulani popiera Janusza Palikota| date = 19 April 2015| publisher = YouTube| language = pl| access-date = 19 April 2015}}</ref> In the same year, in the [[2015 Polish parliamentary election|parliamentary election]] he again supperted Lassota's candidature, congratulating him after obtaining a seat in the [[Sejm]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://twitter.com/JerzyVetulani/status/659065039496835072| title = Cieszę się z sukcesu...| last = Vetulani| first = Jerzy | publisher = Twitter| date = 27 October 2015| language = pl| access-date = 27 October 2015}}</ref>

In the 2000s he lectured regularly at several colleges in Kraków. He was a professor of the Małopolska Higher Vocational School of J. Dietl in Kraków, where he taught classes in cosmetology and dietetics (neurobiological aspect) and the School of Medicine in English at the [[Jagiellonian University Medical College|Jagiellonian University Collegium Medicum]]. He also lectured at the Faculty of Applied Psychology at the [[Jagiellonian University]] and at the [[Pontifical University of John Paul II]].

In 2010 he performed in a [[lip dub]] created by the community of Jagiellonian University. He appeared in its opening sequence as a grandfather of a little girl, the main character in the clip.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qw1Pvj91PJU| title = Jagiellonian University LipDub| publisher = YouTube| access-date = 11 April 2012| date = 22 June 2010}}</ref> Also from 2010 Vetulani regularly appeared on the stage of the talking magazine ''[[Gadający Pies]]'' (''The Talking Dog''), of which he became one of the main attractions and recognizable signs over time. One of the showrunners, Maciej Piotr Prus, described Vetulani as “the star of the first magnitude”, adding that all participants were always waiting for his speeches. Vetulani compared the atmosphere of ''The Talking Dog'' to the ambience present in the beginnings of Piwnica pod Baranami.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://krakow.wyborcza.pl/krakow/1,44425,11025265,Kulturalne_Odloty__Pies_pieknie_eklektyczny.html| title = Kulturalne Odloty: Pies pięknie eklektyczny| last = Niemczyńska| first = Małgorzata I.| publisher = [[Gazeta Wyborcza]] Kraków| date = 25 January 2012| language = pl| access-date = 13 May 2012}}</ref> In his short presentations, the scientist used obscene humor and vulgarity, which some considered to be a violation of good taste, but most of the audience was enthusiastic to this kind of performance. In 2013 Vetulani performed and was the executive producer of the short film ''Hydrophobia'',<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.filmpolski.pl/fp/index.php?film=1240735| title = ''Hydrofobia''| publisher = Filmpolski.pl| access-date = 10 March 2017}}</ref> a [[mockumentary]] that ridiculed social phobias and premiered also at ''The Talking Dog''. He co-created the performance ''Dreams Music'' directed by Czet Minkus, where he performed alongside [[Jan Peszek]] and [[Agata Zubel]];<ref>{{cite web| url = http://ninateka.pl/film/dreams-music13-czeslaw-minkus| title = ''Dreams Music'13''| publisher = Ninateka| access-date = 13 April 2017}}</ref> the show was presented on December 19, 2013, in the Małopolska Garden of Art (MOS). In 2010 and 2015 Vetulani performed with [[Leszek Długosz]] with a concert program ''Rozumie mój'' (''Oh, My Mind''), in which poetry sung by Długosz was exchanged with Vetulani's neuroscience commentary.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://vetulani.wordpress.com/2010/12/16/piekna-impreza/| title = Piękna impreza| publisher = vetulani.wordpress.com| date = 16 December 2010| access-date = 7 April 2017| last = Vetulani| first = Jerzy}}</ref> On December 31, 2014, he was appointed a member of the Program Board of the {{ill|Station in Rome of the Polish Academy of Sciences|pl|Polska Akademia Nauk – Stacja Naukowa w Rzymie}}.

Since 2014, he has been supporting auctions of the [[Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity]]; he devoted for auctions signed books and the opportunity to meet him at coffee or dinner.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://aukcje.wosp.org.pl/jerzy-vetulani-mozg-z-osobista-dedykacja-i915799| title = ''Mózg'' z osobistą dedykacją| publisher = aukcje.wosp.org.pl| date = 13 January 2014| access-date = 16 January 2016| language = pl| archive-date = 10 April 2019| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190410141344/http://aukcje.wosp.org.pl/jerzy-vetulani-mozg-z-osobista-dedykacja-i915799| url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://aukcje.wosp.org.pl/neurobiologiczna-kolacja-z-vetulanim-i1271538| title = Neurobiologiczna kolacja z Vetulanim| publisher = aukcje.wosp.org.pl| date = 12 January 2015| access-date = 16 January 2016| language = pl| archive-date = 10 April 2019| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190410124828/http://aukcje.wosp.org.pl/neurobiologiczna-kolacja-z-vetulanim-i1271538| url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://aukcje.wosp.org.pl/neurobiologiczna-kawa-z-vetulanim-i2711237| title = Neurobiologiczna kawa z Vetulanim| publisher = aukcje.wosp.org.pl| date = 24 January 2016| access-date = 16 January 2016| language = pl| archive-date = 10 April 2019| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190410125146/http://aukcje.wosp.org.pl/neurobiologiczna-kawa-z-vetulanim-i2711237| url-status = dead}}</ref> In 2015 and 2017 he was in the Honorary Committee of the [[Parada Równości]] (Equality Parade, [[pride parade]] held in Warsaw).<ref>{{cite web| url = http://paradarownosci.eu/aktualnosci/nasz-komitet-honorowy-rosnie-w-sile| title = Nasz Komitet Honorowy rośnie w siłę!| publisher = paradarownosci.eu| date = 26 May 2015| access-date = 16 January 2016| language = pl}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Following the rule of [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] party in Poland he sharply criticized their reforms, expressing his support for some of the actions undertaken by the [[Committee for the Defence of Democracy]]; he participated in the protest against taking over public media by the ruling party in January 2016, saying that he “had the fantastic atmosphere of the event: in spite of the January chill – the crowds of old and young full of energy, each step you meet a friend (...). The event had both high civic and social value”, although he kept certain criticism to the form of the protest.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://opinie.wp.pl/prof-jerzy-vetulani-zachowanie-polskiego-rzadu-jest-niekatolickie-6072300849713793a| title = Prof. Jerzy Vetulani: zachowanie polskiego rządu jest niekatolickie| publisher = wp.pl| last = Koszkowska| first = Ewa| date = 25 December 2016| access-date = 10 March 2017| language = pl}}</ref> Invited by students, he participated in the protest on the Main Market Square in Kraków in January 2017.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dgmuUHArEPE| title = Jerzy Vetulani na proteście studenckim w Krakowie| publisher = YouTube| date = 25 January 2017| language = pl}}</ref> He also supported [[Abortion in Poland#Black Protest|Black Protest]], what he manifested by simply wearing black clothes. In November 2016, an exhibition of photographs by {{ill|Adam Golec|pl|Adam Golec}} from Vetulani's eightieth birthday party, that Vetulani organized in his home hosting at once around one hundred and eighty people, was opened at the [[Galeria Olympia]]. During the party, Golec portrayed the participants in a specially prepared mini-studio, on the background painted by {{ill|Iwona Siwek-Front|pl|Iwona Siwek-Front}}.

=== Accident and death ===
[[File:Rakowice Cemetery, grave of Jerzy Vetulani (Polish biochemist), 26 Rakowicka street, Kraków, Poland.jpg|thumb|200px|The grave of Jerzy and Maria Vetulani at the [[Rakowicki Cemetery]] in Kraków]]
On March 2, 2017, in the evening, Vetulani, who was at the age of 81, was hit by an automobile at the pedestrian crossing receiving serious injuries. Vetulani was walking home from his regular place of work, the Institute of Pharmacology of the Polish Academy of Sciences, taking a route he knew very well. Directly after the accident he was put into a pharmacological coma, and his condition was determined as severe but stable.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://krakow.wyborcza.pl/krakow/7,44425,21448446,prof-jerzy-vetulani-mial-wypadek-w-ciezkim-stanie-trafil-do.html| title = Prof. Jerzy Vetulani miał wypadek. W ciężkim stanie trafił do szpitala| publisher = krakow.wyborcza.pl| date = 3 March 2017| access-date = 10 March 2017| language = pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Profesor Vetulani wciąż jest w śpiączce. Został potrącony na przejściu dla pieszych|publisher=TVN24.pl|access-date=3 May 2017|url=http://www.tvn24.pl/krakow-prof-vetulani-wciaz-w-spiaczce-zostal-potracony-na-przejsciu,726036,s.html| language = pl}}</ref> He was being treated at the Emergency Medicine Rescue and Disaster Center at the Szpital Uniwersytecki (University Hospital) in Kraków, under the supervision of the team of Professor [[Jerzy Wordliczek]].

Vetulani's health did not improve and he died in the hospital on April 6, 2017.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://krakow.wyborcza.pl/krakow/7,44425,21603879,prof-jerzy-vetulani-nie-zyje.html| title = Prof. Jerzy Vetulani nie żyje| date = 7 April 2017| access-date = 7 April 2017| publisher = krakow.wyborcza.pl| language = pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.tvn24.pl/krakow,50/krakow-w-wieku-81-lat-zmarl-professor-jerzy-vetulani,730133.html| title = W wieku 81 lat zmarł professor Jerzy Vetulani | date = 7 April 2017| access-date = 7 April 2017| publisher = tvn24.pl| language = pl}}</ref> He was buried on April 18, 2017, in the Avenue of the Meritorious at the [[Rakowicki Cemetery]] in Kraków. [[Aleksander Janicki (artist)|Aleksander Janicki]], visual artist and Vetulani's friend was the master of the ceremony which was carried out in a secular rite. Among the speakers at the funeral were Mayor of Kraków [[Jacek Majchrowski]], president of the Polish Academy of Learning {{ill|Andrzej Białas|pl|Andrzej Białas}}, Member of the Sejm [[Józef Lassota]], and also friends and family of Jerzy Vetulani.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://krakow.wyborcza.pl/krakow/7,44425,21652700,pogrzeb-prof-vetulaniego-do-zobaczenia-w-miejscu-w-ktorego.html?disableRedirects=true|title=Pogrzeb prof. Vetulaniego. "Do zobaczenia w miejscu, w którego istnienie nie wierzyłeś"|publisher=wyborcza.pl|access-date=18 April 2017| language = pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.gazetakrakowska.pl/wiadomosci/krakow/a/pacyfistyczna-piosenka-zabrzmiala-na-pogrzebie-niezwyklego-naukowca,11998902/| title = Pacyfistyczna piosenka zabrzmiała na pogrzebie niezwykłego naukowca| publisher = Gazeta Krakowska| date = 19 April 2017| access-date = 30 May 2018| language = pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cXwUPsW09lw| title = Pogrzeb prof. Jerzego Vetulaniego| publisher = Miasto Kraków| date = 18 April 2017| access-date = 30 May 2018| language = pl}}</ref>

His wife Maria Vetulani died on 21 September 2017.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.nekrologi.net/nekrologi/maria-vetulani/51198281| title = Necrology of Maria Vetulani| publisher = Dziennik Polski| date = 23 September 2017| access-date = 25 September 2017| language = pl}}</ref>

== Views ==
As crucial in shaping his worldview, Jerzy Vetulani pointed ''[[The Naked Ape]]'' by English zoologist [[Desmond Morris]]. He first came across Morris's work in Cambridge in 1967 and said: “Thanks to this book for the first time I saw that you could approach a man like a normal animal species. (...) I realized at that time how ridiculous is a man who, as an animal instead of on all fours, is walking on two legs. How funny we look, hairless almost all over the body. (...) I also got rid of the belief in the superuniqueness of Homo sapiens”.{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| pp=125–126}} Vetulani defined the source of happiness and fulfillment of life, considered from the perspective of biology, as the immortalization of one's own genes by passing them on to the next generations. He often referred to [[Theodosius Dobzhansky]]'s well-known quotation and the title of one of Dobzhansky's works: ''[[Nothing in Biology Makes Sense Except in the Light of Evolution]]''. Vetulani was close to the philosophy of [[utilitarianism]] of [[John Stuart Mill]]; he said: “Moral is what serves to increase the happiness of mankind. There is only one problem – unfortunately we have no way of summing up that happiness”.{{sfn|Rotkiewicz|2015| pp=133–134}} He was a fan of [[fantasy]] and [[science fiction]] literature, and especially of authors such as [[Ursula K. Le Guin]], [[Isaac Asimov]], [[J. R. R. Tolkien]] and [[George R. R. Martin]]. As his motto he adopted a phrase from Asimov's ''[[Foundation (Isaac Asimov novel)|Foundation]]'': “May your moral sense never lead you to make a wrong decision”.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://wyborcza.pl/magazyn/7,124059,21608877,mama-powiedziala-mi-obys-byl-dobry-i-szczesliwy-co-prof.html| title = "Mama powiedziała mi: Obyś był dobry i szczęśliwy". Co prof. Jerzy Vetulani mówił o swoim życiu, pasjach i nauce?| publisher = wyborcza.pl| date = 7 September 2017| access-date = 8 May 2017| language = pl}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* Awards of the Scientific Secretary of the Polish Academy of Sciences (team, 1972, 1977);
* Awards of the Faculty of Medicine of the Polish Academy of Sciences (as team leader, 1982, 1986, 1992);
* [[Medal of the 40th Anniversary of People's Poland]] (1984);
* Gold Badge of the Copernicus Polish Society of Naturalists (1986);
* International {{ill|Anna-Monika Prize|de|Anna-Monika Prize|display=1}} (2nd class, 1983);
* Gold badge of the Polish Copernicus Society of Naturalists (1986);
* an honorary member of the Indian Academy of Neurosciences (1988);
* [[Cross of Merit (Poland)|Gold Cross of Merit]] (1990);
* {{ill|Nicolaus Copernicus Scientific Award|pl|Nagroda Naukowa im. Mikołaja Kopernika|display=1}} (1996);
* an honorary member of the Polish Copernicus Society of Naturalists (1996);
* Jerzy Konorski Award granted by the [[Polish Neuroscience Society]] (2001);
* [[Prime Minister of Poland]] Award for the entirety of his scientific achievements (2003);
* [[Order of Polonia Restituta|Knight's Cross of Polonia Restituta]] (2004);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://isap.sejm.gov.pl/DetailsServlet?id=WMP20050010006 | title = M.P. z 2005 r. Nr 1, poz. 6| access-date = 5 February 2013 | publisher = isap.sejm.gov.pl| language = pl}}</ref>
* Honoris causa degree from the [[Medical University of Silesia]] (2004);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://test-naukawpolsce.pap.pl/aktualnosci/news,17487,gothert-i-vetulani-doktorami-honoris-causa-slaskiej-akademii-medycznej.html| title = Gothert i Vetulani doktorami honoris causa Śląskiej Akademii Medycznej| access-date = 12 April 2012| author = Marek Błoński| publisher = Nauka w Polsce| date = 17 June 2004| language = pl}}</ref>
* Jędrzej Śniadecki Medal for the entirety of his research in the field of psychopharmacology (2006);
* an honorary member of [[Polish Neuroscience Society]] (2007);
* Honoris causa degree from the [[Medical University of Łódź]] (2008);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.umed.pl/pl/index1.php?dir=akt&mn=ummedia&code=9| title = Wideo z uroczystości wręczania doktoratów honorowych| access-date = 12 April 2012| publisher = Uniwersytet Medyczny w Łodzi| language = pl| archive-date = 21 September 2011| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110921060454/http://www.umed.pl/pl/index1.php?dir=akt&mn=ummedia&code=9| url-status = dead}}</ref>
* {{ill|Honoris Gratia Medal|pl|Odznaka „Honoris Gratia”|lt=Honoris Gratia badge}} from the mayor of the Royal Capital City of Kraków (2009);
* Kraków Book of the Month (January 2011);
* Zbyszek Thielle Award from Polish Drug Policy Network “for uncompromising support with his scientific authority for the efforts to humanize Polish drug policy, for attitude of deep understanding of the problems of people who use and depend on psychoactive substances, for work and activities for the introduction of medical cannabis and the defense of the civil rights of its users” (2011);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://vetulani.wordpress.com/2011/06/30/otrzymalem-nagrode-im-zbyszka-thiellego/| title = Otrzymałem Nagrodę im. Zbyszka Thiellego| access-date = 12 April 2012| author = Jerzy Vetulani| publisher = vetulani.wordpress.com| date = 30 June 2011| language = pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cUrSd4ZgrK8| title = Wideo z gali wręczania nagrody| access-date = 12 April 2012| publisher = YouTube| date = 4 July 2011| language = pl}}</ref>
* Rationalist of the Year from Polish Rationalists Society (2012);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.psr.org.pl/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=168%3Aprof-vetulani-zostal-racjonalista-roku-2011&Itemid=101&lang=pl| title = Prof. Vetulani został Racjonalistą Roku 2011| access-date = 12 April 2012| author = Katarzyna Bena| publisher = Polskie Stowarzyszenie Racjonalistów| date = 30 March 2012| language = pl}}</ref>
* Special Award for in the competition "Science Popularizer" organised by [[Polish Press Agency|PAP]] and the [[Ministry of Science and Higher Education (Poland)|Ministry of Science and Higher Education]] the entirety of his popular work; justification stated that the scientist “brings to the reader not only the latest findings of neuroscientists, but also the socially important conclusions of these studies” (2012);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://naukawpolsce.pap.pl/aktualnosci/news,393192,rozstrzygnieto-viii-edycje-konkursu-popularyzator-nauki.html| title = Rozstrzygnięto VIII edycję konkursu "Popularyzator Nauki"| access-date = 31 December 2012 | publisher = Nauka w Polsce| date = 5 December 2012| language = pl}}</ref>
* ''[[Gazeta Krakowska]]'' Man of the Year (2014);<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.gazetakrakowska.pl/artykul/3348475,oto-nasi-ludzie-roku-dobrzy-madrzy-dzielni-zdjecia,id,t.html?cookie=1| title = Oto nasi Ludzie Roku: dobrzy, mądrzy, dzielni [ZDJĘCIA]| publisher = Gazeta Krakowska| date = 27 February 2014| access-date = 13 May 2014| language = pl}}</ref>
* [[Medal for Long Marital Life]] (2014);
* Starost of [[Gorlice]] Award (2016);<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Vetulani ze statuetką Mosty Starosty 2016|url=http://halogorlice.info/powiat/item/1111-professor-vetulani-ze-statuetka-mosty-starosty-2016|author=Tomasz Stasiowski|agency=halogorlice.info|date=30 January 2016|access-date=31 January 2016}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
* Honorary Fellow of the [[Oxford Neurological Society]] (2017).<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://neurologicalsociety.org/prof-jerzy-vetulani-awarded-honorary-fellowship/|title=Prof Jerzy Vetulani Awarded an Honorary Fellowship {{!}} Oxford Neurological Society|date=27 March 2017|work=Oxford Neurological Society|access-date=29 March 2017|archive-date=29 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170329051449/http://neurologicalsociety.org/prof-jerzy-vetulani-awarded-honorary-fellowship/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
